text:
elena: Quick follow-up from the model-versioning RFC — I sketched a lightweight change to rollout metadata to handle soft anchors and migration hints. Want feedback before I file a proper PR.

chris: high-level — please outline the concrete fields. soft anchors sound useful but we need clear semantics for fallback behavior. :thinking: 

elena: Agreed. Proposal (very short): introduce `anchor_mode` (values: `hard` | `soft`), `anchor_version`, `migration_policy` (auto|manual|notify), `compatibility_tags` (list), `expiry_ts` (optional). `soft` means we will attempt to serve `anchor_version` but allow compatible newer versions per policy.

maria: How do we decide "compatible"? We need a machine-readable contract, not just tags. Maybe a `compat_matrix` pointer? Or keep tags + eval-set checks.

elena: My thought: tags are coarse (e.g., `tokenizer-stable`, `kv-size-unchanged`, `schema-v2`). The control plane will consult the model catalog for a last-passing-eval per tag. If a candidate model matches all tags, it's eligible under `soft` anchor. If not, fallback.

sophia: Sounds workable. Suggest adding `fallback_variant` string (model id or alias) so services don't have to compute fallbacks at call time. Also, `migration_hint` with optional `gradual_percent` to enable staged rollouts.

elena: Nice — updated minimal example metadata:```yaml
anchor_mode: soft
anchor_version: model-7.2.1
migration_policy: auto
compatibility_tags:
  - tokenizer-stable
  - kv-cache-compatible
fallback_variant: model-7.1.x
migration_hint:
  gradual_percent: 10
expiry_ts: "1699999999"
```

chris: Two tradeoffs: (1) complexity in runtime to evaluate tags vs trusting catalog precomputation, (2) semantics for `auto` migration — do we allow minor metric regressions? We should bind `auto` to a metric threshold in the rollout metadata or reference an `eval_profile_id`.

maria: +1 on `eval_profile_id`. That makes the decision deterministic. Example: `migration_policy: auto:eval_profile:latency-1,threshold:-2%` — but that starts to become nested. We could instead add `eval_profile` and `acceptance_criteria` fields.

elena: I prefer flat fields to keep schemas easy to parse. Proposal: `eval_profile_id` (string) and `acceptance_criteria` (comma-separated list strings, e.g., `perplexity:-1%,latency:+5%`). Yes it's a bit ugly but keeps JSON/YAML flat.

sophia: If we go with `acceptance_criteria` string we need clear parsing rules. Also need a plan for backfills: if a customer pins an old model that no longer exists in catalog, what happens? We should add `anchor_source` (hosted|dedicated|private) and `allow_orphan_anchor` boolean to control strictness.

elena: Good call. I'll add `anchor_source` and `allow_orphan_anchor`. Default `false` — system will reject anchors not in catalog unless explicitly allowed.

chris: Operational concerns: when a soft anchor allows newer models, billing/compatibility lifecycles matter. We should log any auto-upgrades and expose an audit trail `upgrade_events` (but that can be a separate telemetry table, not in the rollout metadata).

maria: For rollout UI, we want to show a simple state machine: anchored -> evaluating -> promoted -> rolled-back. The metadata fields you propose map well to that.

elena: Action items: (1) I'll draft a PR with the flat schema (fields: `anchor_mode`, `anchor_version`, `anchor_source`, `allow_orphan_anchor`, `migration_policy`, `eval_profile_id`, `acceptance_criteria`, `compatibility_tags`, `fallback_variant`, `migration_hint`, `expiry_ts`). (2) chris/maria can propose exact parsing rules for `acceptance_criteria` and `migration_hint` subfields. (3) ops: we'll add telemetry hooks for any automatic promotions.

sophia: LGTM. Also, add a short migration helper in the console: "convert hard anchors to soft with explicit fallback" — should reduce customer ops. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/rollout-schema-v2 -> staging (sha: abcd1234)

chris: One last nit — rename `anchor_version` -> `pinned_version`? I actually prefer `pinned_version` because "anchor" was overloaded in prior docs. Thoughts?

elena: I purposely picked `anchor` to emphasize soft/hard semantics, but `pinned_version` is more familiar. Let's pick `anchor_alias` as a compromise? Actually that might be confusing. I'm ok with `pinned_version` if everyone prefers the familiarity.

maria: `pinned_version` is fine, but keep `anchor_mode` as the policy. So the pair becomes `pinned_version` + `anchor_mode`. That reads well.

elena: OK final call: use `pinned_version` + `anchor_mode`. I'll update the PR. Thanks everyone — I'll tag you on the draft.

sophia: Thanks — excited to see this land.

elena: filing the PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfc/pull/492
